problem_statement: The LVC store API lacks a zero-allocation range-scan capability. Callers must either iterate the full keyspace or use Consumer boxing, both of which violate the allocation-free hot-path invariant. R-003 adds StoreVisitor-based ascending and descending range scans for SINGLE and DOUBLE stores with optional prefix filtering via DirectBuffer, covering empty, single-key, full-keyspace, and reverse-scan scenarios.
assumptions: StoreVisitor.java stub and default LvcStore range method signatures already exist in the worktree from prior QA-author work; the implementer must provide allocation-free concrete SINGLE and DOUBLE store overrides.
Prefix filtering uses a DirectBuffer key prefix to avoid Consumer boxing; no secondary indexes or sorted-by-value queries are introduced.
The existing JMH benchmark harness supports new @Benchmark methods for range variants without build-system changes beyond method additions.
All concrete SINGLE and DOUBLE store classes are reachable under core/src/main/java/ or a sibling module visible via the multi-module Gradle build.
The alloc gate in qa/smoke.sh exercises JMH benchmark output and will detect any visitor hot-path allocations introduced by the range scan.
Empty-range guard (fromSlot > toSlot) must be an explicit no-op; the default implementations do not already enforce this.

design_contract.public_api: interface StoreVisitor (@FunctionalInterface) { void visit(int slotId); } in com.joshorig.ull.lvc.api; LvcStore declares: default void ascendingRange(int fromSlotInclusive, int toSlotInclusive, StoreVisitor visitor), default void ascendingRange(int fromSlotInclusive, int toSlotInclusive, DirectBuffer prefix, StoreVisitor visitor), default void descendingRange(int fromSlotInclusive, int toSlotInclusive, StoreVisitor visitor), default void descendingRange(int fromSlotInclusive, int toSlotInclusive, DirectBuffer prefix, StoreVisitor visitor). Concrete SINGLE and DOUBLE store classes override these with allocation-free seqlock-safe iteration.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: core/ owns StoreVisitor interface and LvcStore API default stubs. Concrete SINGLE and DOUBLE store classes own the range-scan hot path. conformance-tests/ owns cross-variant behavioural contracts via RangeApiTestSupport. benchmarks/ owns JMH range-scan benchmark methods for single/double and direct/mmap variants.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Range scans read each slot under the existing per-slot seqlock; iteration order is slot-id ascending or descending; no global lock is acquired. Prefix-filter comparison is performed inline before calling visitor.visit(); no internal buffer reference is held across the visit() call boundary.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: Range scan is strictly read-only; it must not write, checkpoint, advance any durable cursor, or mutate journal state during or after a scan.
hard_constraints: Zero allocations on the visitor hot path after @Setup / after store construction; verified by smoke.sh alloc gate.
No Consumer<>, lambda captures of heap objects, or autoboxing in the scan loop.
No sorted-by-value queries, composite keys, or secondary indexes.
Prefix filtering must use DirectBuffer index-based comparison only; no byte[] copies.
ascendingRange and descendingRange must be inclusive on both bounds.
Empty range (fromSlot > toSlot) must be an explicit no-op yielding zero visits and no exception.
forbidden_alternatives: Consumer<Integer> or BiConsumer callbacks on the hot path.
Collecting slot IDs into a List or array before visiting.
Introducing a sorted secondary index for range queries.
Using reflection or dynamic dispatch inside the scan loop.
Calling DirectBuffer.getBytes() into a heap array inside the prefix-filter path.
Advancing any durable cursor or journal position during a scan.
acceptance_tests: Empty range (fromSlot > toSlot) on SINGLE and DOUBLE stores yields 0 visits with no exception.
Single-key range (fromSlot == toSlot) on SINGLE and DOUBLE stores yields exactly 1 visit with the correct slot ID.
Full-keyspace ascending range on SINGLE and DOUBLE stores visits all slot IDs in strictly ascending order.
Full-keyspace descending range on SINGLE and DOUBLE stores visits all slot IDs in strictly descending order.
Prefix-filter ascending range on SINGLE and DOUBLE stores skips non-matching slots with no Consumer boxing or heap allocation.
smoke.sh alloc gate reports zero allocations for range-scan JMH benchmark methods on single/double direct/mmap variants.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh both exit 0 after implementation.

risk_register: Concrete SINGLE/DOUBLE store class locations may differ from core/src/main/java/ root — implementer must locate them via Gradle subproject source sets before writing overrides.
Prefix-filter DirectBuffer comparison may inadvertently call getBytes() into a heap array — implementer must use index-based comparison methods exclusively.
Seqlock retry loop in range scan may spin under heavy concurrent writer contention — implementer must cap retries or delegate to the existing store retry protocol.
JMH benchmark methods for range scan may not be discovered by smoke.sh if naming deviates from project convention — verify naming against existing benchmark class patterns before submitting.
Empty-range guard (fromSlot > toSlot) may be omitted causing a backward scan or ArrayIndexOutOfBounds — must be explicitly tested in qa-author and verified in review.
Default LvcStore range method stubs from prior worktree work may conflict with new concrete overrides — implementer must reconcile stubs to avoid duplicate method compilation errors.
Reverse-scan (descending) inclusive-bound off-by-one at toSlotInclusive is a common inversion error — conformance tests must assert the exact final slot is included.
